ov: Predatory relatives of corals and jellyfish, named after the anemone flower. Each is a single polyp, usually fixed to a hard surface, with a ring of stinging tentacles around a central mouth. Many get extra food from algae living in their cells.

why.et: Eaten in a few places, such as a curry soup in parts of Thailand and in Zhejiang, China.

len: Mostly 1.5–10 cm tall; a few reach 1 m
df: Fish, crustaceans and other small animals caught with stinging tentacles, and in many species food made by algae in their cells.
fx: They creep around on their base, so slowly that the movement shows only in time-lapse.
One magnificent sea anemone lived for eighty years in captivity.
